messages.content: I defined my own ObjectMapper bean and now spring.jackson.* properties are ignored. Why, and how do I keep them?

JacksonAutoConfiguration creates its ObjectMapper with @ConditionalOnMissingBean, so your bean replaces it and nothing applies spring.jackson.* to yours. Instead of defining an ObjectMapper, either:
- define a Jackson2ObjectMapperBuilderCustomizer bean to adjust Boot's mapper, or
- build yours from the injected Jackson2ObjectMapperBuilder (builder.build()), which already has the properties applied.
(In Boot 4 with Jackson 3 the equivalent customizer is JsonMapperBuilderCustomizer.)
My library's auto-configuration must run after DataSourceAutoConfiguration but its @ConditionalOnBean(DataSource.class) never matches. What's wrong?

@ConditionalOnBean is evaluated against beans registered so far, so ordering matters. Declare the order explicitly with @AutoConfiguration(after = DataSourceAutoConfiguration.class). Also make sure the class is registered as an auto-configuration (AutoConfiguration.imports) and not picked up by component scanning, because component-scanned classes are processed before auto-configurations and the ordering then has no effect.
Why should auto-configuration classes not be in a package covered by component scanning?

If @ComponentScan finds them they are processed as ordinary @Configuration classes, before auto-configuration. Their @ConditionalOnMissingBean / @ConditionalOnBean checks then run too early and the after/before ordering in @AutoConfiguration is ignored, so they can create beans that should have backed off or fail to back off. Keep them in a separate package and register them only via META-INF/spring/org.springframework.boot.autoconfigure.AutoConfiguration.imports.
How do I write a custom condition that activates a configuration only when either of two properties is set?
How do I unit-test my own auto-configuration without starting an application?

Use ApplicationContextRunner:

```java
new ApplicationContextRunner()
  .withConfiguration(AutoConfigurations.of(MyAutoConfiguration.class))
  .withPropertyValues("my.enabled=true")
  .withUserConfiguration(UserBeans.class)
  .run(ctx -> assertThat(ctx).hasSingleBean(MyService.class));
```
Use FilteredClassLoader to simulate a missing class for @ConditionalOnClass tests, and WebApplicationContextRunner for web conditions.
What's the difference between @ConditionalOnClass on a class and on a @Bean method, and why does it matter?

On the class, Boot reads the annotation from bytecode with ASM before loading the class, so referring to a missing class is safe. On a @Bean method inside an already-loaded class, the method's return/parameter types may be resolved when the class is introspected, which can throw NoClassDefFoundError. Put class conditions on the configuration class (or a nested static @Configuration class) rather than on bean methods that reference optional types.
Two auto-configured beans of the same type exist and injection fails with NoUniqueBeanDefinitionException. How do you resolve it without changing the library?

Options, from least to most invasive:
1. Inject by qualifier/name: @Qualifier("beanName").
2. Define your own @Primary bean of that type (often delegating to one of the existing ones).
3. Inject List<T> or ObjectProvider<T> and pick explicitly.
4. Exclude the auto-configuration that contributes the unwanted bean.
How do I publish configuration metadata so IDEs autocomplete my custom properties?

Add spring-boot-configuration-processor as an annotation processor (optional/compileOnly dependency). It generates META-INF/spring-configuration-metadata.json from @ConfigurationProperties classes, including Javadoc descriptions and defaults from field initialisers. Add hints or deprecations manually in META-INF/additional-spring-configuration-metadata.json.
What does @ImportAutoConfiguration do and when would you use it?

It imports a specific set of auto-configuration classes regardless of @EnableAutoConfiguration. Test slices use it (e.g. @WebMvcTest imports only web-related auto-configurations). You'd use it in tests or in a minimal context where you want a precise list of auto-configurations instead of everything on the classpath.
How does Boot decide the order of BeanPostProcessors and why can an early-initialised bean break @Transactional or @Async?

BeanPostProcessors are instantiated before regular beans, ordered by PriorityOrdered, Ordered, then the rest. If a BeanPostProcessor (or a @Bean method on a configuration class that defines one, when not static) depends on a regular bean, that bean is created before all post-processors are registered, so it misses proxying for @Transactional/@Async. Spring logs 'Bean X is not eligible for getting processed by all BeanPostProcessors'. Fix: declare BeanPostProcessor @Bean methods static and inject dependencies lazily (ObjectProvider).
A property set in application-prod.yml inside the jar is not overriding application.yml outside the jar. Why?

Since 2.4, files outside the jar take precedence over files inside it, and profile-specific files override non-profile files from the same location. The order is: jar application.yml < jar application-prod.yml < external application.yml < external application-prod.yml. So an external application.yml beats the jar's application-prod.yml. Move the override into an external application-prod.yml or set it via environment/command line.
How do I bind a Map<String, List<Endpoint>> from YAML with keys containing dots?

Wrap map keys in brackets so the dots are kept:

```yaml
app:
  routes:
    "[api.v1]":
      - url: http://a
    "[api.v2]":
      - url: http://b
```
Bind with @ConfigurationProperties("app") record AppProps(Map<String, List<Endpoint>> routes). Without brackets, Boot treats dots as nesting and strips special characters from keys.
How do I bind Duration and DataSize properties and what units are assumed?

Declare fields as java.time.Duration or org.springframework.util.unit.DataSize. Values like 30s, 5m, 2h, 500ms or 10MB, 1GB are parsed. A bare number defaults to milliseconds for Duration and bytes for DataSize; change the default unit with @DurationUnit(ChronoUnit.SECONDS) or @DataSizeUnit(DataUnit.MEGABYTES). ISO-8601 (PT30S) also works.
How do I provide secrets from Kubernetes mounted files to Spring Boot?

Use config trees: spring.config.import=optional:configtree:/etc/secrets/. Each file name becomes a property name and its content the value, e.g. /etc/secrets/db/password -> db.password. Filenames with dots work too (spring.datasource.password).
How do I change properties after startup without restarting the app?

Plain Spring Boot doesn't re-bind properties at runtime. Options:
- Spring Cloud Context: @RefreshScope beans plus the /actuator/refresh endpoint (or Spring Cloud Bus) re-bind @ConfigurationProperties and recreate refresh-scoped beans.
- Store the dynamic value in an external store (DB, feature-flag service) and read it per request.
Log levels are an exception: they can be changed via /actuator/loggers.
What's the difference between spring.config.location and spring.config.additional-location?

spring.config.location replaces the default search locations (classpath:/, classpath:/config/, file:./, file:./config/ ...). spring.config.additional-location keeps the defaults and adds more locations with higher precedence. Both must be set before the environment is prepared, i.e. as system property, env var or command-line argument, not in application.properties.
I need to run custom logic to add a property source before the application context is created. Where do I hook in?

Implement EnvironmentPostProcessor and register it in META-INF/spring.factories under org.springframework.boot.env.EnvironmentPostProcessor. It runs after Boot loads config data and can add or reorder PropertySources. Use Ordered to position it relative to Boot's own processors. For loading from a new source type, implement ConfigDataLocationResolver/ConfigDataLoader instead so it works with spring.config.import.
Why does my @Value field come out null in a constructor?

Field injection happens after the constructor runs. Inject via the constructor instead: MyBean(@Value("${x}") String x). Also check the bean isn't created with new (not managed by Spring) and that the class isn't a static field or a BeanFactoryPostProcessor @Bean (those are created before property placeholders are resolved for regular beans).
How do I validate nested @ConfigurationProperties objects?
How do profiles interact with spring.profiles.include and why can't I set spring.profiles.active in application-dev.properties?

Since 2.4, spring.profiles.active and spring.profiles.include may only appear in non-profile-specific documents; setting them in application-dev.properties fails with InvalidConfigDataPropertyException, because profile files can't activate further profiles after profile resolution. Use spring.profiles.group in application.properties to have one profile pull in others.
My @ControllerAdvice handler for MethodArgumentNotValidException is never called when problem details are enabled. Why?

With spring.mvc.problemdetails.enabled=true Boot registers a ProblemDetailsExceptionHandler (a ResponseEntityExceptionHandler) that already handles MethodArgumentNotValidException. If both advices can handle it, ordering decides. Either extend ResponseEntityExceptionHandler yourself and override handleMethodArgumentNotValid (Boot then backs off its own), or give your advice a higher precedence with @Order(Ordered.HIGHEST_PRECEDENCE).
How do I add a request/response logging filter that runs before Spring Security?
Requests with large JSON bodies fail with 413 or connection reset. Which limits apply?

For Tomcat: server.tomcat.max-swallow-size and server.tomcat.max-http-form-post-size (forms), plus multipart limits spring.servlet.multipart.max-file-size and max-request-size. A reverse proxy (nginx client_max_body_size) often imposes its own limit too. For WebFlux, raise spring.codec.max-in-memory-size (default 256KB) when decoding large bodies into memory.
How do I version a REST API in Spring Boot 4?

Spring Framework 7 / Boot 4 adds first-class API versioning. Configure a version resolution strategy (header, query parameter, path segment or media type parameter), e.g. spring.mvc.apiversion.use.header=API-Version, then map handlers with @GetMapping(path = "/users", version = "1.1"). Before Boot 4 you implement it manually with separate paths (/v1/...), headers in @RequestMapping(headers=...), or a custom RequestCondition.
How do I stream a large file download without loading it into memory?
Why do my Server-Sent Events connections close after 30 seconds?

Spring MVC async requests time out according to spring.mvc.async.request-timeout or the container default (Tomcat ~30s). Create SseEmitter with an explicit timeout (new SseEmitter(0L) for no timeout, or a long value), send periodic heartbeat events so proxies don't drop idle connections, and complete/remove emitters on onCompletion/onTimeout/onError.
How do I make Spring Boot correctly generate https redirect URLs behind a TLS-terminating load balancer?

Set server.forward-headers-strategy=native (use the container's support, Tomcat RemoteIpValve) or framework (Spring's ForwardedHeaderFilter). Boot then honours X-Forwarded-Proto/Host/Port or Forwarded headers so redirects and ServletUriComponentsBuilder produce https URLs. Only trust these headers from your proxy (server.tomcat.remoteip.internal-proxies).
How do I declare an HTTP interface client in Spring Boot?
How do I configure timeouts for RestClient in Spring Boot 3.4+?

Set spring.http.client.connect-timeout and spring.http.client.read-timeout, which Boot applies to the auto-configured ClientHttpRequestFactory used by RestClient.Builder and RestTemplateBuilder. Choose the implementation with spring.http.client.factory (jdk, http-components, jetty, reactor, simple). For per-client values build a ClientHttpRequestFactory via ClientHttpRequestFactoryBuilder and pass it to builder.requestFactory(...).
WebFlux controller calls a blocking JDBC repository. What goes wrong and how do you fix it?

Blocking calls on Netty event-loop threads stall all requests on that loop; throughput collapses under load. Fixes: use a reactive driver (R2DBC); or wrap the call in Mono.fromCallable(...).subscribeOn(Schedulers.boundedElastic()); or switch to Spring MVC with virtual threads if the stack is mostly blocking. BlockHound can detect such calls in tests.
I'm getting LazyInitializationException when serialising an entity to JSON in a REST controller. What are the correct fixes?

The lazy association is accessed after the persistence context closed (open-in-view disabled or the access happens outside the transaction). Fixes:
- Fetch what you need inside the transaction: JOIN FETCH in JPQL, @EntityGraph on the repository method.
- Map to a DTO/projection inside the service layer instead of serialising entities.
Avoid enabling open-in-view or hibernate.enable_lazy_load_no_trans as fixes; they hide N+1 queries.
A @Transactional method calls another @Transactional(propagation = REQUIRES_NEW) method in the same class, but no new transaction starts. Why?

Spring's transactions are proxy-based. A call via this.method() bypasses the proxy, so the annotation on the inner method is ignored and it runs in the outer transaction. Move the inner method to another bean, inject the bean's own proxy (self-injection via @Lazy or ObjectProvider), or use TransactionTemplate programmatically.
Why does my transaction not roll back when a checked exception is thrown?

By default @Transactional rolls back only on RuntimeException and Error. Use @Transactional(rollbackFor = Exception.class) or throw an unchecked exception. Also check the exception actually propagates out of the proxied method (not swallowed by a catch block).
How do I detect and fix N+1 queries in a Spring Data JPA app?

Detect: enable logging.level.org.hibernate.SQL=debug, or Hibernate statistics (spring.jpa.properties.hibernate.generate_statistics=true), or assert query counts in tests (e.g. datasource-proxy). Fix: JOIN FETCH queries, @EntityGraph(attributePaths = "orders"), DTO projections, or batch fetching (spring.jpa.properties.hibernate.default_batch_fetch_size=50) to turn N queries into N/50.
How do I configure two DataSources with JPA in one Spring Boot app?

Boot auto-configures only one. Define both yourself:
- Two DataSourceProperties + DataSource beans (mark one @Primary), bound with @ConfigurationProperties("app.datasource.first") etc.
- Two LocalContainerEntityManagerFactoryBean beans built with EntityManagerFactoryBuilder, each with its own packages.
- Two JpaTransactionManager beans.
- @EnableJpaRepositories(basePackages=..., entityManagerFactoryRef=..., transactionManagerRef=...) per package.
Use @Transactional("secondTransactionManager") for the non-primary one.
How does optimistic locking work with Spring Data JPA and how do I handle conflicts?

Add a @Version field to the entity. Hibernate includes it in the UPDATE's WHERE clause and increments it; if no row matches, it throws OptimisticLockException, translated to ObjectOptimisticLockingFailureException. Handle it by retrying (e.g. Spring Retry @Retryable on the service method, with a fresh transaction per attempt) or returning 409 Conflict to the client.
Hikari logs 'Connection is not available, request timed out after 30000ms'. How do you diagnose it?

The pool is exhausted. Check:
- Connections held too long: long transactions, open-in-view, slow queries, external calls inside @Transactional.
- Connection leaks: set spring.datasource.hikari.leak-detection-threshold=2000 to log stack traces of leaked connections.
- Pool size vs concurrency: maximum-pool-size (default 10) versus thread count, especially with virtual threads, which can create far more concurrent requests than the pool.
Monitor hikaricp.connections.* metrics via Actuator.
How do I use projections to fetch only some columns with Spring Data JPA?
What is the difference between spring.jpa.hibernate.ddl-auto values, and which should production use?

none: do nothing; validate: check schema matches entities and fail if not; update: alter schema to add missing tables/columns (never drops, can make poor choices); create: drop and create on startup; create-drop: also drop on shutdown (default for embedded DBs). Production should use none or validate with schema managed by Flyway or Liquibase.
How do I publish domain events from an aggregate and handle them after commit?

Extend AbstractAggregateRoot and call registerEvent(...); Spring Data publishes the events when the aggregate is saved via a repository. Handle them with @TransactionalEventListener(phase = AFTER_COMMIT) so side effects (emails, messages) happen only if the transaction commits. Note that in AFTER_COMMIT listeners, further DB writes need a new transaction (REQUIRES_NEW).
How do I implement the transactional outbox pattern with Spring Boot?

In the same transaction as the business change, insert the event into an outbox table. A separate process reads unsent rows and publishes them to the broker, marking them sent; consumers must be idempotent since delivery is at-least-once. Implementations: a @Scheduled poller with SELECT ... FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED, Debezium CDC on the outbox table, or Spring Modulith's event publication registry.
Liquibase/Flyway migrations run but Hibernate validation fails at startup with missing columns. What ordering issue might exist?

Boot runs Flyway/Liquibase before the EntityManagerFactory via a dependency, but this only holds for the auto-configured beans. If you defined your own EntityManagerFactory or DataSource, or the migration targets a different DataSource/schema, the order or target may differ. Check spring.flyway.schemas/default-schema, that migrations ran against the same DB (flyway_schema_history), and that spring.jpa.defer-datasource-initialization isn't combined with migrations.
Each test class creates a new Spring context and the suite is slow. How do you make contexts reuse?

Spring's TestContext framework caches contexts keyed by configuration. Different @MockitoBean/@MockBean sets, @TestPropertySource values, active profiles, or @DirtiesContext create new contexts. Standardise: a shared abstract base test class with the same annotations, minimise per-class mocks and properties, avoid @DirtiesContext, and use slices where possible. Check cache stats with logging.level.org.springframework.test.context.cache=debug.
How do I share one Testcontainers container across many test classes?

Declare the container as a @Bean with @ServiceConnection in a @TestConfiguration and @Import it into tests; the context cache then reuses it while the context is reused. Or use a static container started once in a base class (singleton pattern) instead of @Container per class. testcontainers.reuse.enable=true additionally keeps containers between runs locally.
How do I test that my REST client correctly handles a 500 from an external API?
How do I test Spring Security rules on a controller?
What does MockMvcTester add over MockMvc in Spring Boot 3.4?

MockMvcTester (Spring Framework 6.2) wraps MockMvc with AssertJ-style assertions and no checked exceptions:

```java
assertThat(mvc.get().uri("/users/1"))
  .hasStatusOk()
  .bodyJson().extractingPath("$.name").isEqualTo("Ana");
```
Boot 3.4 auto-configures it in @WebMvcTest/@AutoConfigureMockMvc when AssertJ is present.
How do I test code that uses @Async or @Scheduled deterministically?

Test the business logic directly (call the method synchronously, not through the scheduler). For integration tests: replace the TaskExecutor with a SyncTaskExecutor in a @TestConfiguration so @Async runs inline, or wait for side effects with Awaitility (await().atMost(5, SECONDS).untilAsserted(...)). Disable scheduling in most tests by putting @EnableScheduling on a configuration class guarded by a property.
How do I test a Kafka consumer with Spring Boot?

Use @SpringBootTest with Testcontainers' KafkaContainer and @ServiceConnection (or @EmbeddedKafka from spring-kafka-test). Produce a message with KafkaTemplate, then assert the effect with Awaitility. Set spring.kafka.consumer.auto-offset-reset=earliest so the consumer reads messages produced before partition assignment.
@DataJpaTest passes on H2 but production on PostgreSQL fails. How do you make repository tests trustworthy?

Test against the real database engine: Testcontainers PostgreSQLContainer with @ServiceConnection plus @AutoConfigureTestDatabase(replace = Replace.NONE). H2 differs in SQL dialect, native queries, constraints, JSON types, locking and sequences. Run Flyway migrations in the test too so the schema matches production.
How do I override a single bean for an integration test without affecting other tests' context cache?

Use @MockitoBean / @TestBean (Spring Framework 6.2) for that test class — this does create a distinct context, so group tests needing the same overrides into one base class. Alternatively define the alternative in a @TestConfiguration with spring.main.allow-bean-definition-overriding=true, or make the production bean configurable by property so tests switch behaviour without replacing beans.
After upgrading to Spring Security 6, my H2 console and some POST endpoints return 403. What changed?

Likely causes:
- CSRF is enabled by default; POSTs without a token are rejected. Disable it for stateless APIs (http.csrf(c -> c.disable())) or ignore specific matchers.
- authorizeHttpRequests now applies to all dispatcher types, including ERROR and FORWARD, so error pages may be denied; permit /error.
- H2 console needs frame options set to sameOrigin and its path permitted and CSRF-ignored (PathRequest.toH2Console()).
How do I configure two security filter chains: one stateless JWT for /api/** and one form-login for the rest?
How do I map roles from a Keycloak JWT into Spring Security authorities?
How do I enable method-level security and what changed from @EnableGlobalMethodSecurity?

Use @EnableMethodSecurity (Spring Security 5.6+); @EnableGlobalMethodSecurity is deprecated. @EnableMethodSecurity enables @PreAuthorize/@PostAuthorize by default (prePostEnabled=true), uses the AuthorizationManager API, and supports meta-annotations. Enable @Secured or JSR-250 with securedEnabled/jsr250Enabled.
How do I secure Actuator endpoints so health is public but everything else needs ADMIN?
Where should I store password hashes and which encoder should I use?

Use PasswordEncoderFactories.createDelegatingPasswordEncoder(), which defaults to bcrypt and prefixes hashes with {bcrypt}, so you can migrate algorithms later (argon2, scrypt, pbkdf2). Never store plain or reversibly encrypted passwords. Implement UserDetailsPasswordService to upgrade old hashes transparently on login.
How do I propagate the security context to @Async methods?

The SecurityContext is thread-local by default and lost on another thread. Wrap the executor with DelegatingSecurityContextAsyncTaskExecutor, or set SecurityContextHolder strategy to MODE_INHERITABLETHREADLOCAL (only safe without thread pools). With Micrometer context propagation, a ContextPropagatingTaskDecorator on the executor also carries the context.
How do I implement OAuth2 login with GitHub in Spring Boot?

Add spring-boot-starter-oauth2-client and configure the registration:

```yaml
spring:
  security:
    oauth2:
      client:
        registration:
          github:
            client-id: ${GITHUB_ID}
            client-secret: ${GITHUB_SECRET}
```
GitHub is a well-known provider, so no provider URLs are needed. Enable http.oauth2Login(Customizer.withDefaults()). The redirect URI defaults to {baseUrl}/login/oauth2/code/github and must be registered in the GitHub app.
How do I add a custom metric that counts business events with tags?

Inject MeterRegistry and create a counter:

```java
Counter.builder("orders.placed").tag("channel", channel).register(registry).increment();
```
Keep tag values low-cardinality (no user IDs). Alternatively use the Observation API (Observation.createNotStarted("orders.place", registry).observe(...)) to get metrics and a trace span at once.
How do I add percentile histograms for HTTP latency for Prometheus?

management.metrics.distribution.percentiles-histogram.http.server.requests=true publishes histogram buckets so Prometheus can compute any quantile with histogram_quantile(). Limit bucket ranges with management.metrics.distribution.minimum-expected-value / maximum-expected-value. Client-side percentiles (percentiles=0.95) can't be aggregated across instances.
How do I group health indicators so readiness depends on the database but liveness doesn't?

```properties
management.endpoint.health.group.readiness.include=readinessState,db
management.endpoint.health.group.liveness.include=livenessState
```
Liveness should not include external dependencies: a DB outage would otherwise make Kubernetes restart every pod, which doesn't fix the DB.
How do I mark the app as not ready while it warms a cache at startup?

Boot sets readiness to ACCEPTING_TRAFFIC only after ApplicationRunners/CommandLineRunners complete, so do the warm-up in an ApplicationRunner. To change it manually, publish AvailabilityChangeEvent.publish(context, ReadinessState.REFUSING_TRAFFIC) and later ACCEPTING_TRAFFIC.
How do I export traces via OTLP to an OpenTelemetry collector?

Add spring-boot-starter-actuator, io.micrometer:micrometer-tracing-bridge-otel and io.opentelemetry:opentelemetry-exporter-otlp, then:

```properties
management.otlp.tracing.endpoint=http://collector:4318/v1/traces
management.tracing.sampling.probability=1.0
```
Default sampling is 0.1. Logs get traceId/spanId in the MDC automatically.
Trace IDs disappear in logs from @Async methods and CompletableFuture. Why?

The tracing context lives in thread-locals. Boot propagates it to its auto-configured executor only when a context-propagating TaskDecorator is used; set spring.task.execution... or register ContextPropagatingTaskDecorator as a bean (Boot 3.2+ applies it to the auto-configured executors). Plain CompletableFuture.supplyAsync uses the ForkJoin common pool, so pass a wrapped executor (ContextExecutorService.wrap(...)).
How do I add custom data to /actuator/info?
How do I reduce metric cardinality from http.server.requests caused by URIs with IDs?

Boot tags with the URI template (/users/{id}), not the actual path, when requests map to handlers. High cardinality happens with unmapped paths or clients building URIs from strings (RestTemplate with concatenated URLs). Use URI templates in clients (uri("/users/{id}", id)), and add a MeterFilter.maximumAllowableTags(...) or deny filter as a safety net.
How should I set JVM memory in a container for a Spring Boot app?

Modern JVMs read cgroup limits. Use -XX:MaxRAMPercentage=75 rather than a fixed -Xmx so heap scales with the container limit, leaving room for metaspace, thread stacks, direct buffers and code cache. Paketo buildpacks run a memory calculator that sets these flags automatically. Set requests=limits for memory in Kubernetes to avoid OOM kills.
How do I shut down gracefully in Kubernetes without dropping requests?

Use server.shutdown=graceful (default from 3.4) and a preStop hook that sleeps a few seconds (e.g. sleep 10) so endpoints are removed from the Service before SIGTERM arrives. Make terminationGracePeriodSeconds larger than preStop + spring.lifecycle.timeout-per-shutdown-phase. Readiness turns to REFUSING_TRAFFIC during shutdown automatically.
Native image build fails at runtime with ClassNotFoundException for a class used via reflection. How do you fix it?
What limitations of Spring AOT/native should you design around?

The bean set is fixed at build time ('closed world'): @Profile and @Conditional on properties are evaluated at build time, so changing profiles at runtime doesn't change beans. Reflection, resources, proxies and serialization need hints. Classpath scanning at runtime and dynamic class generation don't work. Some libraries lack native support. Build times and memory use are high.
How do I reduce Spring Boot startup time on the JVM without native images?

Options: CDS (Boot 3.3+, with -Dspring.context.exit=onRefresh training run), Spring AOT on the JVM (spring.aot.enabled=true with AOT-processed jar), lazy initialization, excluding unused auto-configurations, avoiding wide classpath scanning, and using Project Leyden's AOT cache on newer JDKs. Measure with the /actuator/startup endpoint (BufferingApplicationStartup) to find slow beans.
How do I find which beans are slow during startup?
How do I run Spring Boot behind a reverse proxy under a sub-path like /app?

Either set server.servlet.context-path=/app so the app itself serves under /app, or keep the app at / and have the proxy send X-Forwarded-Prefix: /app with server.forward-headers-strategy=framework, so generated links include the prefix. Mixing a proxy rewrite with no prefix header breaks redirects and links.
@Scheduled jobs run multiple times when I scale to three instances. How do you ensure only one runs?

@Scheduled is per-JVM. Use a distributed lock: ShedLock (@SchedulerLock with a JDBC/Redis LockProvider) or Spring Integration's JdbcLockRegistry. For heavier needs use Quartz in clustered JDBC mode or move the job to an external scheduler (Kubernetes CronJob).
Two @Scheduled methods block each other. Why?

The default scheduler has a single thread (spring.task.scheduling.pool.size=1), so a long task delays others. Increase the pool size, offload work with @Async, or enable virtual threads (spring.threads.virtual.enabled=true), which gives scheduled tasks their own virtual threads.
How do I retry a failed Kafka message and send it to a dead-letter topic after N attempts?
How do I make a RabbitMQ consumer idempotent and avoid losing messages when the app crashes?

Use manual or auto acknowledgment mode (default AUTO acks only after the listener returns successfully, so a crash redelivers). Make processing idempotent by storing processed message IDs (unique constraint) in the same DB transaction as the business change. Configure a dead-letter exchange plus retry interceptor (spring.rabbitmq.listener.simple.retry.*) so poison messages don't loop forever.
When should you use virtual threads and when are they harmful?

Good: blocking I/O-heavy request handling (JDBC, HTTP calls) where you'd otherwise need large thread pools. Watch out for: pinning in synchronized blocks around I/O on JDK < 24 (use ReentrantLock or upgrade), unbounded concurrency overwhelming downstream resources such as the connection pool (bound with semaphores), and ThreadLocal-heavy code creating many copies. CPU-bound work gains nothing.
How do I apply backpressure-like limits to an external API when using virtual threads?

Virtual threads remove the thread-pool cap, so add an explicit limit: a Semaphore around the call, Resilience4j Bulkhead (SemaphoreBulkhead) or RateLimiter, and timeouts on the client. Also size the HTTP client's connection pool deliberately.
How do I add circuit breaking and retries to an outbound call in Spring Boot?
How do I process events within a modular monolith asynchronously but reliably?

Spring Modulith: publish events with ApplicationEventPublisher inside the transaction and handle them with @ApplicationModuleListener (async, transactional, after commit). The event publication registry persists each publication and marks it complete when the listener succeeds, so incomplete ones can be republished after a crash.
Upgrading from Boot 2.7 to 3.x, the app compiles but fails with 'jakarta.servlet.Filter not found' from a library. What's going on?

A dependency is still compiled against javax.* (Java EE) APIs. Boot 3 needs Jakarta EE 9+ (jakarta.*). Upgrade the library to its Jakarta-compatible version (often a new major or a -jakarta classifier). As a last resort, transform the bytecode with the Eclipse Transformer, but treat that as temporary.
What property changes are common when upgrading Spring Boot 2.x to 3.x?

Examples: spring.redis.* -> spring.data.redis.*; spring.data.cassandra.* -> spring.cassandra.*; management.metrics.export.<registry>.* -> management.<registry>.metrics.export.*; server.max-http-header-size -> server.max-http-request-header-size; spring.sql.init replaced spring.datasource.initialization-mode earlier (2.5). Add spring-boot-properties-migrator temporarily to get a report at startup.
After moving to Boot 3, Hibernate fails on a sequence-based ID with 'sequence does not exist' or IDs jump by 50. Why?

Hibernate 6 changed ID generation defaults: GenerationType.AUTO now uses a SequenceStyleGenerator with a dedicated sequence per entity (entity_name_seq) and an allocation size of 50 with pooled optimizers. Create the sequences (e.g. via Flyway) with INCREMENT BY 50, or set @SequenceGenerator(allocationSize = 1) to match old sequences, or use IDENTITY explicitly.
How do you approach upgrading a large app from Spring Boot 2.3 to 3.5?

Upgrade one minor at a time is ideal, but at least go to 2.7 first: fix deprecation warnings, config file processing changes (2.4), spring.sql.init (2.5), path matching changes (2.6, PathPatternParser default). Then 3.0: Java 17, javax->jakarta, Security 6, Hibernate 6, removed deprecations, trailing slash. Then 3.x minors with release notes. Tools: OpenRewrite's Spring Boot migration recipes, spring-boot-properties-migrator, and a full test suite.
Spring Boot 2.6 apps started failing with 'The dependencies of some of the beans form a cycle'. What changed and how should you fix it?

Since 2.6, circular references are prohibited by default. Fix the design: break the cycle by extracting shared logic into a third bean, using events, or constructor injection with ObjectProvider/@Lazy on one side. spring.main.allow-circular-references=true restores the old behaviour but only hides the problem.
Spring Boot 2.6 broke springfox Swagger with a NullPointerException in documentationPluginsBootstrapper. Why?

2.6 switched Spring MVC's default path matching to PathPatternParser, which springfox doesn't support. Workaround: spring.mvc.pathmatch.matching-strategy=ant_path_matcher. Better: replace springfox (unmaintained) with springdoc-openapi.
What should you know about Jackson 3 when moving to Spring Boot 4?

Jackson 3 uses new packages (tools.jackson instead of com.fasterxml.jackson, though annotations stay in com.fasterxml.jackson.annotation), JsonMapper is the main type, and some defaults changed (e.g. dates are no longer written as timestamps). Customize with JsonMapperBuilderCustomizer instead of Jackson2ObjectMapperBuilderCustomizer. Boot 4 can still run Jackson 2 for compatibility, but plan to migrate.
Why did my imports of RestTemplateBuilder or auto-configuration classes break in Spring Boot 4?

Boot 4 split spring-boot-autoconfigure into technology-specific modules (e.g. spring-boot-restclient, spring-boot-jdbc, spring-boot-webmvc), and many classes moved to new packages. Use the matching starters (spring-boot-starter-restclient etc.) so the right modules are on the classpath, and update imports. Test slices also moved into technology-specific test modules.
Startup fails with 'Failed to configure a DataSource: url attribute is not specified'. What are the possible causes?

DataSourceAutoConfiguration activated because a JDBC dependency (often transitively via JPA) is present but no URL is set and no embedded database is on the classpath. Fix by setting spring.datasource.url, checking the right profile/config file is actually loaded, adding H2 for local use, or excluding DataSourceAutoConfiguration if the app doesn't need a database.
The app starts but endpoints return 404 although controllers exist. What do you check?

1. Controllers outside the main class's package (not scanned).
2. @Controller returning views instead of @RestController/@ResponseBody.
3. Context path or servlet path set (server.servlet.context-path, spring.mvc.servlet.path).
4. Trailing slash in the request (no longer matched since 3.0).
5. spring-boot-starter-web missing (WebFlux or non-web app instead).
Check mappings at /actuator/mappings or in the DEBUG log of RequestMappingHandlerMapping.
A bean is created twice — once by component scanning and once by a @Bean method — and startup fails. How do you fix it?

Since 2.1 bean definition overriding is disabled, so duplicate names fail with BeanDefinitionOverrideException. Remove one of the definitions: drop @Component on the class or remove the @Bean method, or rename one if two beans are really intended. Enabling spring.main.allow-bean-definition-overriding=true is a last resort.
Memory grows steadily in a Spring Boot service until OOM. How do you investigate?

Check heap metrics (jvm.memory.used) to see heap vs non-heap growth. Capture a heap dump (/actuator/heapdump or -XX:+HeapDumpOnOutOfMemoryError) and analyse in Eclipse MAT for dominators. Usual suspects: unbounded caches (use Caffeine with maximumSize), static collections, ThreadLocals in pools, Hibernate first-level cache in long transactions/batches, high-cardinality metrics. For non-heap growth check metaspace (classloader leaks with devtools/dynamic proxies) and direct buffers (Netty).
Why might @Cacheable not cache anything?

- @EnableCaching missing.
- Self-invocation: the method is called from the same class, bypassing the proxy.
- The method isn't public or the bean isn't Spring-managed.
- The key differs per call (e.g. includes objects without equals/hashCode).
- unless/condition expressions exclude results, or the cache manager is NoOpCacheManager (spring.cache.type=none).
How do I debug which property source a value came from?

GET /actuator/env/<property.name> shows the effective value and every property source that defines it, in precedence order (enable the endpoint and set management.endpoint.env.show-values=when-authorized to see values in 3.0+). In code, iterate ConfigurableEnvironment.getPropertySources().
Logback configuration in logback.xml ignores Spring profiles and properties. Why?

logback.xml is loaded by Logback before Spring's Environment exists. Name the file logback-spring.xml so Spring Boot loads it, which enables <springProfile name="prod"> blocks and <springProperty> to read properties from the Environment.
Jackson serialises LocalDateTime as an array of numbers. How do you fix it?

That happens when an ObjectMapper without the JavaTimeModule or with WRITE_DATES_AS_TIMESTAMPS is used, typically a manually created new ObjectMapper(). Use Boot's auto-configured mapper (it registers jackson-datatype-jsr310 and disables timestamps by default) or set spring.jackson.serialization.write-dates-as-timestamps=false. Jackson 3 (Boot 4) writes ISO strings by default.
Requests hang under load and thread dumps show all Tomcat threads waiting in HikariPool.getConnection. What's the root cause and fix?

More concurrent requests need a DB connection than the pool provides (default max 10 vs 200 Tomcat threads), and each request holds a connection too long. Shorten connection hold time (no remote calls inside transactions, disable open-in-view), add indexes for slow queries, size the pool to what the DB can handle, and set connection-timeout low so requests fail fast instead of piling up.
Why is my @EventListener not invoked for ApplicationStartingEvent?

ApplicationStartingEvent (and environment-prepared/context-initialized events) fire before the ApplicationContext and its beans exist, so bean-based @EventListener methods can't receive them. Register the listener via SpringApplication.addListeners(...) or META-INF/spring.factories under org.springframework.context.ApplicationListener.
How would you structure configuration for an app deployed to dev, staging and prod on Kubernetes?

Keep defaults in application.yml inside the jar, environment differences in application-<env>.yml or (better) environment variables/ConfigMaps, and secrets via mounted files with spring.config.import=configtree:. Activate the environment with SPRING_PROFILES_ACTIVE. Avoid putting secrets in the jar or in plain env var listings, and validate required properties with @Validated @ConfigurationProperties so misconfiguration fails at startup.
When would you choose Spring WebFlux over Spring MVC with virtual threads?

WebFlux fits streaming use cases (SSE, WebSockets with backpressure), gateway/proxy workloads composing many non-blocking calls, and when the whole stack is reactive (R2DBC, reactive drivers). With Java 21+, MVC with virtual threads gives similar scalability for typical blocking I/O apps with simpler code, debugging and stack traces, so it's usually the default choice now.
How do you write a Spring Boot starter for an internal library?

Create two modules: an autoconfigure module (with @AutoConfiguration classes, @ConfigurationProperties, conditions, AutoConfiguration.imports registration and the configuration processor) and a starter module that only has dependencies (the library + autoconfigure). Name it acme-spring-boot-starter (not spring-boot-*). Use @ConditionalOnMissingBean so users can override beans, and test with ApplicationContextRunner.
How do you keep @ConfigurationProperties classes immutable and why?

Use records or final fields with constructor binding (default for a single constructor since 3.0). Immutability avoids accidental runtime mutation from other beans and makes validation happen once at startup. Use @DefaultValue for defaults and Duration/DataSize types for clarity.
How do you implement multi-tenancy with separate schemas in Spring Boot JPA?

Use Hibernate's multi-tenancy: implement CurrentTenantIdentifierResolver (reading the tenant from a request-scoped or ThreadLocal context set by a filter) and MultiTenantConnectionProvider (switching schema with SET search_path or picking a DataSource). Register them via HibernatePropertiesCustomizer. Clear the tenant context after each request, and run migrations per schema (Flyway with multiple schemas).
How do you expose OpenAPI documentation for a Spring Boot 3 REST API?

Add org.springdoc:springdoc-openapi-starter-webmvc-ui (2.x for Boot 3). It generates /v3/api-docs from controllers and serves Swagger UI at /swagger-ui.html. Annotate with @Operation/@Schema for details, group APIs with GroupedOpenApi beans, and permit these paths in Spring Security. springfox does not support Boot 3.
How should database access be designed to avoid long transactions in a request that also calls a slow external API?

Don't hold a transaction across the external call. Split the work: read what you need in a short transaction, call the API outside any transaction, then write results in a second short transaction (use optimistic locking to detect concurrent changes). For reliability across both, use an outbox or saga instead of one long transaction.
How do you implement rate limiting per API key in a Spring Boot service?

Within one instance, use a filter with Bucket4j (token bucket per key, stored in Caffeine). Across instances, back Bucket4j with Redis or use Spring Cloud Gateway's RequestRateLimiter with Redis. Return 429 with Retry-After headers. Prefer enforcing at the gateway/ingress if one exists.
What's the difference between Spring Boot's 'spring.main.web-application-type' values?

servlet: start a servlet web server (Spring MVC). reactive: start a reactive server (WebFlux on Netty). none: no web server, e.g. batch jobs or CLI tools even if web dependencies are on the classpath. If unset, Boot deduces it: servlet if Spring MVC and a servlet container are present, else reactive if WebFlux is present, else none.
How do you run a Spring Batch job on demand from a REST endpoint and not at startup?

Set spring.batch.job.enabled=false so Boot doesn't run jobs at startup. Inject JobLauncher (or JobOperator) and the Job, and launch with unique JobParameters (e.g. a timestamp) from a controller. Use an async TaskExecutor-backed launcher so the HTTP request returns immediately, and expose the JobExecution ID for status polling. Boot 3 needs the batch schema (spring.batch.jdbc.initialize-schema).
